scope: Proposition 3.1 (Short intervals in a rectangle) of the manuscript “The curve scaling limit of half-plane double dimers” (preprints/The-curve-scaling-limit-of-half-plane-double-dimers-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 226 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 2e1bcd39145db94c), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 12. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let Rδ be corner-rooted odd lattice rectangles converging to a fixed nondegenerate rectangle, with two independent uniform dimer covers. Fix an interior longitudinal coordinate c, two positive numbers ρ−, ρ+, and a bounded segment J of the transverse line x = c. The two regions x ≤ c − ρ− and x ≥ c + ρ+ are called the deep regions; if either is disjoint from the rectangle, the events below are empty. The segment J may extend beyond the transverse sides of the rectangle. For each sufficiently small h > 0, partition J into at most CJ /h intervals of length at most h, with endpoints off the graph. Use a seam converging to x = c and the corresponding intervals when necessary. A tested arc is a cycle subarc, in its cycle direction, with one endpoint in each deep region. Let Bδ,h be the event that some partition interval I satisfies at least one of the following conditions: (i) a tested arc α on a cycle g has ιI(α) ̸= 0 and ιI(α) ̸= ιI(g); (ii) tested arcs on two distinct cycles both have nonzero intersection number with I. The arcs may otherwise travel anywhere in the rectangle. Then lim h↓0 lim sup δ↓0 P(Bδ,h) = 0. (17) The conclusion is unchanged by truncating intervals at a transverse side, or by placing their endpoints outside the rectangle.
